title: Latency-Cost decomposition lab notes
body:
Purpose: capture raw ideation and a small prototype spec for a dashboard that breaks down per-invocation and per-token cost + latency contribution. Aim is to produce a lightweight, queryable view product teams can use to triage hot paths (slow tokens, expensive prompts) and to inform Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Context: current console has per-route aggregate cost/latency charts and token inspector prototypes, but customers and SREs want an exploration surface that surfaces: (a) which specific tokens or token ranges add the most tail latency; (b) how much KV cache hits saved in tokens; (c) per-invocation amplification (when a single request causes expensive backend operations). This doc is a working lab: lots of sketches, hypotheses, and a short groomed backlog for a small spike.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Maya (owner), Sofia (pm)
- Eng: Liam (frontend), Ethan (instrumentation)
- SRE/support: Priya Kapoor (oncall) [note: invited but not present for initial brainstorm]

Meeting notes (2025-01-14 brainstorm):
- Quick wins: add a column-level breakdown to existing invocation table showing token-cost and token-latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) that are filterable by model variant.
- Longer scope: an interactive per-invocation timeline that can expand to show token-level sparkline + inferred kernel selection and cache hits.
- Concern: data volume at scale — need retention strategy and sampled traces.

Goals (primary):
1) Make it easy to find "high-leverage invocations" where small prompt edits reduce cost/latency materially.
2) Surface model/runtime causes (quantization vs kernel choice vs batching) for latency spikes.
3) Provide deterministic links from dashboard to replayable traces and to Optimize suggestions.

UX hypotheses (things to validate in spike):
- H1: Engineers will prefer a compact per-invocation row with an expandable token-sparkline over a dense token table for scanning.
- H2: Color-coded token bands (compute-intensive vs i/o-wait vs kv-hit) will speed root-cause triage by ~30% vs raw numbers.
- H3: Allowing users to pin an invocation into a comparison pane (compare two invocations side-by-side) will reduce time-to-resolution on regressions.

Data model / telemetry notes (for Ethan):
- Minimum per-invocation payload: invocation_id, route_id, model_variant, start_ts, end_ts, total_tokens, total_cost_cents, token_timeline: list of (offset, token_text_id, token_latency_ms, token_cost_cents_est, cache_hit_bool, kernel_hint), kernel_hint is optional string (e.g., matmul-int8).
- Sampling: store full token_timeline for 1% of invocations; for the rest store aggregated bands: fast/medium/slow token percentiles + first/last k tokens full.
- Privacy: token_text_id should be hashed/pseudonymized by default unless customer opts in (private deployments).

Wireframe descriptions (sketch to hand off to Liam):
1) Invocation list (compact row): route | invocation id | model variant | total latency (p50/p95) | total cost | token-sparkline (mini) | actions (expand, pin, open-trace)
   - token-sparkline: horizontal sparkline with colored segments; segments represent contiguous token groups; hover reveals tooltip with token offsets and quick stats (avg latency, avg cost, cache-hit rate).
2) Expand panel (below row): three tabs: Timeline (per-token waterfall), Attribution (what proportion of cost/latency attributed to model compute vs I/O vs pre/post processing), Suggestions (Optimize suggestions: reduce context length, enable prefix cache, switch to quantized variant).
3) Comparison pane: drag a pinned row to the compare area; compare pane shows aligned sparklines, side-by-side attribution bars, diff view of prompts (highlighting tokens that cause >2x latency delta).
4) Aggregate view (top-level): heatmap with route x token-position buckets showing average latency and cost per token bucket; filterable by time-window and model variant.

Interaction notes and microflows:
- Drilldown: click sparkline -> open Expand panel -> click token in waterfall -> opens right-hand side mini-trace with kernel events and K/V cache hits.
- Bookmark + share: each pinned comparison generates a sharable URL (retains sampling policy) and creates a lightweight note that can be attached to Jira with one-click.
- Bulk actions: select multiple invocations -> run batch re-eval in sandbox (calls an offline runner), or request Optimize suggestion scan on the selection.

Edge cases / constraints:
- Extremely long outputs (>20k tokens): show aggregated bands and top-15 heaviest tokens only.
- Private deployments: telemetry may be restricted; fall back to aggregate-only views and require customer opt-in for token-level.
- Cost estimation accuracy: token-level cost is an estimate (we attribute compute+memory+io share), include a hover tooltip explaining methodology and +/- error bounds.

Open questions (to resolve before grooming):
- Q1: Sampling policy defaults (1% full token timeline) — should we have tiered sampling based on Dedicated / Enterprise customers? (action: product/eng to propose threshold)
- Q2: How much to pre-compute vs compute on read (band aggregation, p95) — cost/latency tradeoffs for the console backend.
- Q3: What language/tokenization mapping to surface? raw token indices vs human-friendly tokens? (prefer human-friendly but expensive to compute for some legacy models)

Backlog (spike -> MLP roadmap)
- Spike-001 (2 weeks): Instrumentation stub + mock data generator + simple UI prototype (Liam + Ethan) -> JIRA-CORE-1287 (priority: high, owner: Ethan).
- Spike-002 (1 week): Sampling & privacy policy draft + legal check (owner: Maya, collaborators: Legal).
- Design-001 (1 week): Figma wires for compact row + expand panel + compare pane (owner: Liam).
- Eng-ML-Est (3 weeks): Backend aggregation job to precompute token bands and p95 for routes (owner: Platform infra).
- UX-Research (2 weeks): 5 customer interviews to validate H1-H3, prioritize enterprise vs self-serve needs.

Proposed acceptance criteria for MLP (minimum lovable product):
- Users can scan route callbacks and identify top 10 heavy invocations for a time window.
- For a selected invocation user can expand to see per-token sparkline (sampled) and attribution tab.
- Pinned comparison supports at least 2 invocations side-by-side with sharable link.

Design notes and microcopy (notes-to-self):
- Label the sparkline segment tooltip: "tokens 23–36 — avg latency 12ms — cache hits 40% — est cost $0.002"
- Use neutral palette for fast tokens, warm palette (amber/red) for slow/expensive tokens; avoid red unless p99 > SLA.
- Add "why this matters" inline help: short sentence above attribution: "This shows which parts of the response are adding tail latency or unit cost — use suggestions to try cheaper model variants or enable prefix caching."

Testing & metrics (SLOs for new surface):
- Instrument time-to-open (UI) and query latencies; target UI open < 400ms for aggregated row view and <1200ms for expand panel on cached data.
- Track feature usage: pinned comparisons created per week, number of Optimize suggestions launched from the panel, and downstream cost savings (post-change).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Liam: mock up compact-row + expand panel (deliverable: Figma link) by 2025-01-21.
2) Ethan: build a small mock-data generator (node script) and a read-only API endpoint returning sampled token timelines by 2025-01-24.
3) Maya: schedule 5 customer interviews w/ CS to test hypothesis H1 by 2025-01-31.

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally messy — prioritize a working prototype to show to customers rather than a perfect taxonomy. Keep sampling conservative initially to limit storage costs. Follow up with legal on token pseudonymization for hosted API.

Attachments to add to the Drive entry once ready: design frames (Figma), telemetry schema (simple csv), quick demo screencast (mp4), and a small dataset of anonymized invocation traces for UX demos.

Revision log:
- 2025-01-14 created (brainstorm)
- 2025-01-20 added backlog and acceptance criteria after sync with Liam
- 2025-02-02 updated sampling defaults and added test metrics
